observations: Two large white air conditioning units are shown outdoors, one with a visible front grille and the other with a side grille.
The unit on the left (photo 0) has a red circular sticker or label near the bottom, possibly a brand or model identifier, but it is too small to read clearly.
The unit on the right (photo 0) has a visible oval-shaped logo or emblem near the top, but the text is not legible.
In photo 1, the same two units are shown from a different angle; the left unit has horizontal slats and a dark oval feature, possibly a brand logo or vent.
The units appear to be commercial or industrial floor-standing models, not split-systems or window units.
The units are dusty and show signs of outdoor storage; the ground is uneven and wet in places.
No indoor unit is visible, suggesting this may be a standalone unit or the indoor unit is not included.
The seller claims it is a 'Tokunbo Panasonic 10 tonnes' unit, but no Panasonic branding is clearly visible in either photo.
The term '10 tonnes' is unusual for residential AC; it likely refers to cooling capacity in tons, but 10 tons is very large for a single unit unless industrial.
The units appear to be used, with visible wear and dirt, contradicting the claim of 'super clean'.

claims.evidence: No clear Panasonic branding visible in either photo; the logo on the unit is too blurry to read. The '10 tonnes' claim is not verifiable from the photos.
Photo 0 and photo 1 show dust, grime, and outdoor storage conditions; the units are not clean.
No visual proof of testing or operation; no power connection or running state shown.

risks.risk: The unit may not be a Panasonic or may be misrepresented as such.
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the brand name on the unit, preferably on the front or side panel.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic used floor-standing AC, not as a branded Panasonic.

risks.risk: The unit may not be 10 tons in capacity; the claim is likely exaggerated or misstated.
risks.proof: A photo of the model plate or nameplate showing the exact model and cooling capacity (in BTU or tons).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a smaller capacity unit, likely 1-3 tons, as 10 tons is extremely large and rare for a single unit of this type.

risks.risk: The unit may not be working or may have hidden damage (e.g., compressor, fan, refrigerant).
risks.proof: A video clip showing the unit running, with sound and airflow, or a photo of the power connection and control panel.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not working, with a significant discount for unverified functionality.

risks.risk: The indoor unit may be missing or not included, making it non-functional as a complete system.
risks.proof: A photo of the indoor unit or a clear statement from the seller confirming it is included.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as incomplete, with a large discount for missing components.

proof_requests: A clear close-up photo of the brand name and model plate on the unit.
A photo or video showing the unit running with airflow and sound.
A photo of the indoor unit if it is included.
A photo of the power connection and control panel.
response.reason: The identity of the unit cannot be confirmed as Panasonic, and the 10-ton claim is unverifiable. The condition is contradicted by visible dirt, and functionality is unproven. Without proof of brand, capacity, and working condition, a worst-case price cannot be determined.
